Where it began

Rashid Khan was born on 20 September 1998 in Nangarhar province in the east of Afghanistan, into a family from Jalalabad. Part of his boyhood was spent over the border in Pakistan, where he studied computer science at Islamia College in Peshawar, a place his sport helped him win.

His heroes were easy to spot: he shaped his bowling action on Shahid Afridi's and loved the batting of AB de Villiers. At first he was the better batter, but leg-spin soon took over, and in 2014 he caught the eye in Peshawar when the Afghan team came to play there.

The player

He was one of the eleven men who played Afghanistan's first Test, against India in June 2018, and it was a hard welcome: 2 for 154 in the first innings. Eight months later, against Ireland, he became the first Afghan to take five wickets in a Test innings. Then in September 2019, aged 20 years and 350 days, he led his country against Bangladesh. Afghanistan won by 224 runs, he took ten wickets in the match and made a fifty, and nobody had done both in his first Test as captain.

In 6 Tests from 2018 to 2025 he took 45 wickets at 20.44, with a best of 7 for 66, five five-wicket innings and three ten-wicket matches. He captained Afghanistan in 2 Tests, winning one.

What made him special

Leg-spin and an appetite for wickets that seemed to grow with every match. In 2017 he took 7 for 18 against West Indies at Gros Islet, the best one-day figures by a player from an associate nation. In February 2018 he became the youngest bowler to top the world one-day rankings, and he reached 100 one-day wickets in only 44 matches, faster than anyone before him. In December 2020 he was named the T20I Cricketer of the Decade, and in September 2025 he passed Tim Southee to hold the record for the most men's T20I wickets.

Even the best spinner has the odd afternoon when the ball keeps landing in the crowd. England took 110 from his nine overs at the 2019 World Cup, which only proved that he was human after all.

Away from the middle

He was a favourite of franchise cricket around the world. He and Mohammad Nabi were the first Afghans picked in the Indian Premier League, with Sunrisers Hyderabad in 2017, and he later took a hat-trick for Gujarat Titans. He won the Big Bash with Adelaide Strikers, where the crowd took him to its heart, took the first hat-trick in the Caribbean Premier League for Guyana Amazon Warriors, played for Sussex and was the first name picked by Trent Rockets in the first draft for The Hundred. In 2017 he was named Associate Cricketer of the Year.

And finally

His first bowling effort in Test cricket cost 154 runs. Over the rest of his Test career he made exactly 154 runs with the bat, so in the end the books balanced.
